newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA 12.59 PCT 2004 BOND UP IN BRISK TRADE.
newsitem.headline: INDIA 12.59 PCT 2004 BOND UP IN BRISK TRADE.

text.p: The 12.59 percent 2004 and 11.19 percent 2005 Indian government bonds were in demand in afternoon trade Wednesday but other stocks were less active, dealers said.

In latest deals, the 12.59 percent 2004 rose to 107.25 from its previous close of 107.05, while the 11.19 percent 2005, auctioned at par on Monday, was steady at Tuesday's close of 100.50 rupees, dealers said.
"These two bonds are the hot favourites at the moment," said a dealer. "But other stocks are almost unchanged."
He said sellers were quoting 100.70 rupees for the 10.85 percent 2001 and 107.35/40 for the 13.70 percent 1999 but buyers were looking for lower prices in both.
Dealers said call money was in a 7.0-7.5 percent range and there was a firm trend in rates.

"Some of the big lenders are quoting higher as they know that last-minute borrowers will be desperate for funds today," said a dealer. "It is the reporting day tomorrow and one or two banks which have not covered will take funds at any available rate today."

Banks normally report their positions to the central bank on alternate Fridays. This fortnight, they will report their posiitons on Thursday as banks are closed on August 15, the nation's independence day.
